test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. She found it at last.
A. There was no other like it in any of the stores, and she had turned all of them inside out.
B. It was even worthy of The Watch.
C. It surely had been made for Jim and no one else.
D. It was a platinum fob chain simple and chaste in design, properly proclaiming its value by substance alone and not by meretricious ornamentation - as all good things should do.
S2. As soon as she saw it she knew that it must be Jim's.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph revolves around a woman finding a perfect gift for Jim, emphasizing her effort and thoughtfulness.
 
• **Sentence C is the first in the logical sequence** because it introduces the platinum fob chain, its design, and its worth, setting the context for its significance:
 
 
• "It was a platinum fob chain simple and chaste in design, properly proclaiming its value by substance alone and not by meretricious ornamentation - as all good things should do."
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows** as it elaborates on how unique the chain is, reinforcing its importance:
 
 
• "There was no other like it in any of the stores, and she had turned all of them inside out."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D comes next** as it emphasizes how perfectly the chain is suited for Jim, connecting it back to the idea of the gift being special:
 
 
• "It surely had been made for Jim and no one else."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B is the last** in the logical sequence as it highlights the worthiness of the chain and its value, which ties back to the overarching sentiment of admiration and effort:
 
 
• "It was even worthy of The Watch."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **CADB**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"It was a platinum fob chain simple and chaste in design, properly proclaiming its value by substance alone and not by meretricious ornamentation - as all good things should do. There was no other like it in any of the stores, and she had turned all of them inside out. It surely had been made for Jim and no one else. It was even worthy of The Watch."</div
